$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.common.loops. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-EMPTY-B-ANY-NONEMPTY
arms.find: loop is redundant only for a SINGLE-CHARACTER $search — '
arms.replace: loop is redundant for any non-empty $search — '
arms.note: the empty-B message claims the single call does the same work for every non-empty S again, which 'aabb'.replace('ab', '') == 'ab' refutes

arms.name: M-SEAM-BLIND
arms.note: no join can ever re-form S, so arm A claims the two-space squeeze is redundant and the autofix deletes a required loop again

arms.name: M-PIA-OBJLIT-SET-FLAGGED
arms.find: if (isSet && cfg.objectLiteralKind != null && call.children[2].kind == cfg.objectLiteralKind) return null;
arms.note: a `set` whose value argument is an OBJECT LITERAL is matched again at the seam `run` and `fix` share, so the fixer rewrites it to an index assignment Haxe rejects (`No @:arrayAccess function for haxe.ds.Map accepts arguments of String and { ... }`)

arms.name: M-COUNT-CONFLICT-SILENT
arms.note: the per-site conflicting-`using` skip drops the `count()` rewrite silently again, and the `length`-form rewrites in the same file hide it from the ledger

arms.name: M-COUNT-GUARDED-MIS-ATTRIBUTED
arms.find: final accepted: Array<Violation> = keptViolations(collected, edits, violations);
arms.note: the guard's sentence is written on every finding the rule reported again, including the ones the containment filter dropped and the ones no site matched

arms.name: M-VALUE-LOOP-READS-UNSPLICED
arms.find: for (span in readSpans) edits.push({ span: span, text: binder });
arms.note: the X[i] occurrences are left unspliced, so prefer-value-loop rewrites the header into a value loop and the body still reads an index binding that no longer exists, and prefer-keyvalue-loop leaves the element reads it promised to re-spell

arms.name: M-VALUE-LOOP-INDEX-TEXT-BLIND
arms.find: if (OccurrenceScan.referencedInRange(f.source, h.index, bodySpan.from, bodySpan.to, indexSpans, f.inert)) return null;
arms.note: the completeness gate is gone, so prefer-value-loop trusts node walks that prune a macro quotation and deletes an index the quotation still reads

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-LOOP-UNSTABLE
arms.note: a write to X[i] or a push onto X no longer declines, so an element-loop rewrite assigns to a copy or follows the growth a bounded range ignored

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-LOOP-REBIND
arms.note: an X[i] under a nested binder of i is re-spelled as the outer element, and a body reaching the collection as this.X is rewritten

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-LOOP-CLOSURE
arms.note: an X[i] read inside a closure becomes the binder, so a closure run after the loop sees the element of its iteration instead of the slot as it is then

arms.name: M-KV-NOOPENER-BODY-GATES
arms.find: if (!ElementLoopRewrite.bodyAdmitsElementLoop(h, f.source, LENGTH_MEMBER, core)) return null;
arms.note: the no-opener arm stops asking the shared body gates, so a closure, a nested binder or a length change reaches its rewrite

arms.name: M-VALUE-LOOP-BODY-GATES
arms.find: if (!ElementLoopRewrite.bodyAdmitsElementLoop(h, f.source, LENGTH_MEMBER, core)) return null;
arms.note: prefer-value-loop stops asking the shared body gates, so a closure, a nested binder or a length change reaches its rewrite

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-LOOP-NESTED-BINDER
arms.find:
else if (nestingLoopDerives(f.root, forNode, candidate, f))
			'an enclosing or nested indexed loop derives the same element name `$candidate`'
arms.note: an outer and an inner indexed loop that derive one binder are both fixed in one pass, and the inner binder shadows the outer for the whole inner body

arms.name: M-SINGULAR-INNER-WORD
arms.find: final singular: Null<String> = endsWord(name, end) ? singularOfEnding
arms.replace: final singular: Null<String> = end == name.length ? singularOfEnding
arms.note: only the end of a name is read as a plural, so gridLinesVertical has no singular and its loop keeps no binder

arms.name: M-SINGULAR-WORD-END-ANYWHERE
arms.note: every position is a word end, so an s inside a word reads as a plural and nodesPosition becomes nodesPoition

arms.name: M-KV-OPENER-SELF-CALL
arms.note: the opener arm never asks the body's reach, so a callee that grows the collection runs on under the key-value iterator

arms.name: M-VALUE-LOOP-SELF-CALL
arms.find: ElementLoopRewrite.gatedEdits(buildEdits(m, f.source), gate, m.header, m.forSpan, m.decline, out);
arms.note: the value-loop fix never asks the body's reach, so a callee that replaces X[i] after the binder was read, or grows the collection, changes what the loop reads

arms.name: M-KV-NOOPENER-INDEX-ONLY
arms.find: if (LoopScan.countReads(h.body, h.index, core) == reads.length) return null;
arms.note: a loop whose index only ever indexes X is claimed by both prefer-keyvalue-loop and prefer-value-loop, so two autofixes race for one header

arms.name: M-KV-NOOPENER-OPENER-CLAIM
arms.find: if (h == null || LoopScan.opensWithIndexBinding(h.body, h.collection, h.index, core)) return null;
arms.note: a body opening with final v = X[i] that the opener arm declined is picked up by the no-opener arm, which renames the opener initializer into final v = v-binder

arms.name: M-KV-NOOPENER-INDEX-WRITE
arms.note: a body that writes the index is rewritten, and the binder no longer follows the index it was read with

arms.name: M-KV-NOOPENER-SELF-CALL
arms.find: ElementLoopRewrite.gatedEdits(buildReadEdits(r, f.source), gate, r.header, r.forSpan, r.decline, out);
arms.note: the no-opener arm never asks the body's reach, so a callee that replaces X[i] after the binder was read, or grows the field, changes what the loop reads

arms.name: M-KV-NOOPENER-NON-ARRAY
arms.find: if (collectionTypeSource != null && NominalTypes.outerNominalOf(collectionTypeSource, f.typeSyntax) != ARRAY_TYPE) return null;
arms.note: a container resolved to something other than Array is reported with a key-value form it has no iterator for

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-LOOP-UNDERSCORE
arms.note: the private-member prefix stays on the collection name, the singularizer refuses it, and both element-loop rules withhold the rewrite of _points

arms.name: M-KV-NOOPENER-TAKEN-SCOPE
arms.note: the binder name is checked against the loop only, so it shadows a parameter or outer local of the same name for the whole loop

arms.name: M-KV-NOOPENER-TAKEN-MEMBER
arms.note: a binder named like a field of the type is written, shadowing the field for the whole loop

arms.name: M-MAPVALUE-SUBTYPE-REPORT-INDEX
arms.note: the no-null-value census asks the REPORT index for the access-grant and subtype doors, so `hxq lint <one file> --fix` with `resolutionRoots` declared collapses `m.exists(k) ? m[k] : d` into `m[k] ?? d` for a map an unlinted subtype stores a null into — the S177 shape in the redundant-map-exists rule, found by T918's `subtype-map-write` cell

arms.name: M-ULB-WILDCARD-KEY-ADMITTED
arms.note: a key already spelled `_` is judged like any other, so `for (_ in xs)` is reported as unread and a discarded key is taken from redundant-map-iter-key

arms.name: M-ULB-OUTER-WILDCARD-BLIND
arms.note: a body read of an outer `_` is ignored, so the renamed binder captures it

arms.name: M-ULB-SHADOW-COUNTED-AS-READ
arms.note: a read of an inner shadow is left unaccounted, so a binder the body only shadows is kept as though read

arms.name: M-ULB-OUTER-BINDING-AS-SHADOW
arms.note: a read resolving to the loop binder itself counts as a shadow, so a binder read before its re-declaration is renamed

arms.name: M-ULB-INTERP-BLIND
arms.note: occurrences are never accounted for, so a `$i` interpolation read and anything else the tree hides is renamed away

arms.name: M-ULB-INTERP-LITERAL-BLIND
arms.note: an occurrence inside an interpolating literal is trusted once resolved, so a `${i}` read of a shadow no longer refuses

arms.name: M-ULB-COVERAGE-BLIND
arms.note: an occurrence no hit accounts for is trusted, so a read inside a macro reification is renamed away

arms.name: M-ULB-OPAQUE-COND-BLIND
find: if (CondRegionScan.opaqueCondRegionMentioning(body, ctx.source, name, ctx.s.shape) != null) return false;
arms.note: an unparsed `#if` region spelling the name is trusted as empty, although nothing inside it projects for the scan to see

arms.name: M-ULB-NATIVE-BLIND
arms.note: target code pasted as a string is not read, so a binder a `Syntax.code` body names is renamed and only the target build fails

arms.name: M-ULB-UNTYPED-BLIND
arms.note: an untyped subtree is trusted to resolve like typed code, so a binder it mentions is judged by the resolver alone

arms.name: M-ULB-CLOSURE-BLIND
arms.note: a closure mentioning the name is judged by the resolver alone, so a lambda whose own parameter shadows the binder lets the rename through

arms.name: M-ULB-COUNTER-CLAIM-BLIND
arms.note: a loop dead-binder-counter-loop claims is reported too, so one loop has two owners

arms.name: M-MAPITERKEY-UNPROVEN-DROPPED
arms.note: the key prefix is dropped over any iterable, so a Map loop whose body removes an entry switches to the iterator that yields its stale value

arms.name: M-ULB-PATTERN-WILDCARD-UNEXEMPT
arms.note: a `case _:` wildcard pattern counts as a read of an outer `_`, so every loop whose body switches is refused

arms.name: M-ULB-UNBOUND-WILDCARD-ADMITTED
arms.note: a `_` the resolver cannot bind (an inherited field) counts as no read, so the renamed binder captures it

arms.name: M-ULB-FIELD-NAME-AS-READ
arms.note: an object-literal field name spelling the binder counts as a read, so the binder is kept

arms.name: M-ULB-WILDCARD-KEY-VALUE-BLIND
arms.find: if (valueBinder != null && valueSpan != null) valueCandidate(ctx, body, bodySpan, valueBinder.name, valueSpan, out);
arms.note: a loop whose key is `_` is skipped whole, so its unread value binder is fixed by nobody

arms.name: M-MAPITERKEY-MESSAGE-ALWAYS-PROVEN
arms.note: every finding recommends for (v in …), including over a Map where the fix declines because the drop is unsafe

arms.name: M-COMPR-INDEXFILL-NEVER
arms.note: a sequential index fill into the empty array is never folded, which is the rule before it learnt the shape

arms.name: M-COMPR-INDEXFILL-VALUE-UNCHECKED
arms.note: the written value skips the self-reference gate, so `out[j] = out.length` folds to a comprehension reading a different array

arms.name: M-COMPR-INDEXFILL-ANY-START
arms.note: a fill from a non-zero start folds, although its first write leaves slot 0 empty rather than appending

arms.name: M-COMPR-INDEXFILL-ANY-INDEX
arms.note: a write at an index other than the loop binder folds, although it does not append

arms.name: M-COMPR-NESTED-NEVER
arms.note: a nested build is never folded, which is the rule before it learnt the shape

arms.name: M-COMPR-GAP-COMMENT-DROPPED
arms.find: if (!gapped) hoistCommentsIn(new Span(declSpan.to, forSpan.from), ctx, acc);
arms.note: an own-line comment between an adjacent declaration and its loop is swallowed by the merge

arms.name: M-COMPR-NESTED-ANY-LENGTH
arms.note: an outer body holding a statement beyond the inner build folds, and the fix drops that statement

arms.name: M-COMPR-NESTED-PUSH-ANY
arms.note: an outer push of something other than the inner array folds as if it pushed the inner array

arms.name: M-COMPR-NESTED-INNER-UNCHECKED
arms.note: the inner fill may read the inner array it builds, which its comprehension no longer is

arms.name: M-COMPR-NESTED-CHECKS-UNMERGED
arms.note: the inner fill's element and bounds skip the outer self-reference gate, so they may read the outer array being built

arms.name: M-COMPR-NESTED-ASCRIPTION-DROPPED
arms.note: the inner declaration's annotation is dropped where the outer element type does not restate it, which can change the elements' type

arms.name: M-COMPR-GAP-NAME-BLIND
arms.note: a gap statement touching the array is crossed, so an index fill into an array the gap already pushed to no longer starts at slot 0

arms.name: M-COMPR-INDEXFILL-ANY-CONTAINER
arms.find: indexesLikeArray(annotation, ctx.seams.typeSyntax) ? indexFill(loop, name, ctx, acc) : null
arms.note: an index fill into a Map or an @:arrayAccess abstract folds, which does not compile or skips the setter

arms.name: M-COMPR-INDEXFILL-RANGE-UNCHECKED
arms.note: the fill's bound skips the self-reference gate, so `0...out.length` folds against a different array

arms.name: M-COMPR-WELD-BLIND
arms.note: two hoisted comments code separated are welded, and the linter's guard then drops every edit of the rule in the file

arms.name: M-COMPR-NESTED-DECL-COMMENT
arms.note: a comment inside the inner declaration is stranded when the nest dissolves it

arms.name: M-MAPITER-KEYED-NEVER
arms.find: else if (NominalTypes.keyedIterationContainer(iterable, root, shape, declaredTypes, index, file, importMap))
arms.note: a standard map is never a keyed container, so a loop over one the body provably leaves unchanged keeps its discarded key

arms.name: M-MAPITER-REACH-SKIPPED
arms.find: final result: ReachResult = reach.mayMutateNamed(file, name, at, body, MemberTouchScan.mapMethods(shape));
arms.note: a map's key is dropped without asking whether the body changes the map, so a loop that removes an entry starts yielding its stale value

arms.name: M-ULB-KEYED-UNPROVED-DROPPED
arms.find: ValueIterationProof.keyedDecline(built, file, keyed.iterable, keyed.body, s.shape) == null;
arms.note: an unread key over a map is dropped without the reach, so a loop that removes an entry switches to the iterator that yields its stale value

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-SILENT
arms.note: no loop is ever reported, so a proven mismatch between a bound and a length passes unseen

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-FIXED-WRITE
arms.note: an index write refuses a fixed-length construction too, though it never resizes one

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-ARRAY-WRITE
arms.note: an index write past the end of an array is read as keeping its length, though it extends it

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-VECTOR-IMPORT
arms.replace:
typeName == SourceText.lastSegment(path)
|| false && ctx.tree.children.exists(c -> ctx.seams.modulePathKinds.contains(c.kind) && c.name == path)
arms.note: any type spelled `Vector` is read as the fixed-length one, OpenFL's growable `Vector` included

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-FOLD-OFF
arms.note: no bound folds, so `G.N + 1` and `5` compare as different texts though the constant makes them equal

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-RELATED-OFF
arms.find: if (related.exists(name -> mentions(bound, name, owner, isField, s))) return;
arms.note: a bound naming the array or a parallel one (`xs.length - 1`) is compared as unrelated text

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-REACH-IGNORED
arms.find: return k != null && k >= 0 ? k : null;
arms.note: a read of `xs[i + 1]` reaches no further than `xs[i]`, so a pairwise loop one short of the length is reported

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-ADMIT-ALL
arms.note: every occurrence keeps the length, so an array handed to a call or appended elsewhere still counts as proven

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-PUBLIC
arms.find: if (mods.exists(m -> s.visibility.contains(m.kind) && textOf(m, ctx.source) != s.defaultVis)) return null;
arms.note: a public field, which another file may resize, gets a proven length

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-CONFINED-OFF
arms.note: a subtype that appends to the field no longer refuses its proven length

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-EXITS
arms.note: a fill loop that may `continue` past its append is read as appending once per iteration

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-WRITE-READ
arms.find:
&& isRef(node.children[0], name, owner, isField, s)
				&& !isWriteTarget(node, parent, s)
arms.note: a loop that only writes the array is reported as reading it

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-NESTED-FILL
arms.find: if (span == null || (span.from >= fillFrom && span.to <= fillTo)) return;
arms.note: a loop inside the fill loop, reading an array still being filled, is compared with its final length

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-SHADOW
arms.note: a binder taking the array's name no longer refuses it, so the occurrences of the binder count as the array's

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-UNSIZED
arms.note: a comprehension literal counts as a one-element literal

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-STATIC-FILL
arms.note: a static field filled in the constructor, which grows with every instance, gets the fill loop's bound as its length

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-SELF-REF
arms.note: `this.xs` is no occurrence of the field `xs`, so a read through it is missed

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-TYPE-OFF
arms.note: a declared type other than the one the source builds no longer refuses the length

arms.name: M-LOOPBOUND-AHEAD
arms.note: a field's occurrence ahead of a same-named local's declaration is read as the local's, so the field's loop is compared with the local's length

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-DO-WHILE-BODY-LAST
arms.note: a do-while's body is read off its LAST child, its condition, so loop-guard never sees the guard that opens it

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-BODY-STATEMENT-BLOCK-ONLY
arms.note: the LIFT arm takes a statement block alone, so a do-while's body block is never lifted

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-EXPR-BODY-KEPT
arms.note: the MERGE arm reads a do-while's expression-body wrapper as its header, so `do if (c) { … } while (x)` is never merged

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-HEADER-STATEMENT-IF-ONLY
arms.note: a MERGE header must be an if-statement, so a do-while's if-expression header is never merged

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-BRANCH-STATEMENT-BLOCK-ONLY
arms.note: a MERGE header's branch must be a statement block, so a do-while header's block expression is never merged

arms.name: M-MAS-ANY-VALUE
arms.note: a map storing false is read as a set of its keys

arms.name: M-LOOP-SHAPE-COUNT-REDECLARED
arms.replace:
final WHILE_CHILD_COUNT: Int = 2;
	if (loop.kind != s.whileKind || loop.children.length != WHILE_CHILD_COUNT) return null;
arms.note: the rule keeps its own while child count instead of asking LoopScan, so the slot-constant guard finds a second copy of the answer
